nodes.description: Subretinal delivery of an AAV vector carrying CNGA3 under a cone-directed promoter. It restores cone responses, normalises cGMP and delays cone death in the Cnga3 knockout mouse, and has restored photopic vision in day-blind sheep for six years after a single injection. The first-in-human AAV8.CNGA3 dose-escalation trial in nine adults found no substantial safety problem and small gains in acuity and contrast sensitivity. Intravitreal delivery did not achieve clinical rescue in sheep, which is why the route is subretinal. There is no approved gene therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Restoration of cone vision in the CNGA3-/- mouse model of congenital complete lack of cone photoreceptor function.
evidence.snippet: Treated CNGA3(-/-) mice were able to generate cone photoreceptor responses and to transfer these signals to bipolar cells.

evidence.reference_title: Restoration of cone vision in the CNGA3-/- mouse model of congenital complete lack of cone photoreceptor function.
evidence.snippet: Moreover, expression of CNGA3 normalized cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) levels in cones, delayed cone cell death and reduced the inflammatory response of Müller glia cells that is typical of retinal degenerations.

evidence.reference_title: AAV-Mediated Gene Supplementation Therapy in Achromatopsia Type 2: Preclinical Data on Therapeutic Time Window and Long-Term Effects.
evidence.snippet: In summary, we found that the therapeutic time window of opportunity for AAV-mediated Cnga3 gene supplementation therapy in the Cnga3 KO mouse model extends at least to an age of 3 months, but is presumably limited by the condition, number and topographical distribution of remaining cones at the time of treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Gene Augmentation Therapy Restores Retinal Function and Visual Behavior in a Sheep Model of CNGA3 Achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: The rescue effect has so far been maintained for over 3 years in the first-treated animals, with no obvious ocular or systemic side effects.

evidence.reference_title: Six Years and Counting: Restoration of Photopic Retinal Function and Visual Behavior Following Gene Augmentation Therapy in a Sheep Model of CNGA3 Achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: ERG Critical Flicker Fusion Frequency and flicker amplitudes at 30 and 40 Hz showed significant improvement following treatment (p < 0.0001) throughout the study.

evidence.reference_title: Safety and Vision Outcomes of Subretinal Gene Therapy Targeting Cone Photoreceptors in Achromatopsia: A Nonrandomized Controlled Trial.
evidence.snippet: Subretinal gene therapy with AAV8.CNGA3 was not associated with substantial safety problems and was associated with cone photoreceptor activation in adult patients, as reflected by visual acuity and contrast sensitivity gains.

evidence.reference_title: Outer retinal transduction by AAV2-7m8 following intravitreal injection in a sheep model of CNGA3 achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: Intravitreal injection of AAV2-7m8 carrying human CNGA3 in mutant sheep resulted in mild photoreceptor transduction, but did not lead to the clinical rescue of photopic vision, while day-blind sheep treated with a subretinal injection exhibited functional recovery of photopic vision.

nodes.description: Impaired colour discrimination along all three cone axes; most patients cannot distinguish colours at all.

evidence.reference_title: Total colourblindness is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the alpha-subunit of the cone photoreceptor cGMP-gated cation channel.
evidence.snippet: Total colourblindness (OMIM 216900), also referred to as rod monochromacy (RM) or complete achromatopsia, is a rare, autosomal recessive inherited and congenital disorder characterized by photophobia, reduced visual acuity, nystagmus and the complete inability to discriminate between colours.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic phenotypic characteristics and inheritance patterns of patients with achromatopsia at a large academic institution and a review of the literature and gene therapies.
evidence.snippet: All patients experienced difficulties with color vision, 20 of 21 (95.2%) had photosensitivity, and 18 of 21 patients reported congenital nystagmus.

evidence.reference_title: CNGA3 mutations in hereditary cone photoreceptor disorders.
evidence.snippet: The majority of all known CNGA3 mutations (39/46) are amino acid substitutions compared with only four stop-codon mutations, two 1-bp insertions and one 3-bp in-frame deletion.

evidence.reference_title: CNGA3 mutations in hereditary cone photoreceptor disorders.
evidence.snippet: These four mutations account for 41.8% of all detected mutant CNGA3 alleles.

evidence.reference_title: Endoplasmic reticulum stress-associated cone photoreceptor degeneration in cyclic nucleotide-gated channel deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in the cone CNG channel subunits CNGA3 and CNGB3 account for >70% of all known cases of achromatopsia.

nodes.description: Biallelic CNGA3 variants, most of them missense substitutions at residues conserved across the cyclic nucleotide-gated channel family, alter the alpha subunit of the cone CNG channel. The substitutions cluster at the cytoplasmic face of transmembrane segments S1 and S2, in S4, and in the cGMP-binding domain. This is the initiating, cone-autonomous lesion.

evidence.reference_title: Total colourblindness is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the alpha-subunit of the cone photoreceptor cGMP-gated cation channel.
evidence.snippet: In all cases, the segregation pattern of the mutations is consistent with the autosomal recessive inheritance of the disease and all mutations affect amino acids that are highly conserved among cyclic nucleotide gated channels (CNG) in various species.

evidence.reference_title: CNGA3 mutations in hereditary cone photoreceptor disorders.
evidence.snippet: The missense mutations mostly affect amino acids conserved among the members of the cyclic nucleotide gated (CNG) channel family and cluster at the cytoplasmic face of transmembrane domains (TM) S1 and S2, in TM S4, and in the cGMP-binding domain.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of novel mutations by targeted exome sequencing and the genotype-phenotype assessment of patients with achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: The proposed topological model of the CNGA3 polypeptide suggested that the missense mutations primarily affected the transmembrane helix 5 and the cGMP-binding domain, respectively.

nodes.description: Naturally occurring day blindness in the Improved Awassi breed, caused by a stop-codon substitution in ovine CNGA3 and inherited recessively. Affected sheep have severely depressed photopic electroretinogram responses with no retinal degeneration on histology, so cones are present but silent, as in patients. The large eye makes it the model used to develop subretinal AAV delivery.
A small central scotoma with eccentric fixation.

evidence.reference_title: Achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: Achromatopsia is characterized by reduced visual acuity, pendular nystagmus, increased sensitivity to light (photophobia), a small central scotoma, eccentric fixation, and reduced or complete loss of color discrimination.

nodes.description: Targeted deletion of the cone CNG channel alpha subunit. The mouse has no cone-mediated photoresponse with a fully intact rod pathway, fails to transport opsin into cone outer segments, accumulates cGMP, and loses cones progressively from the second postnatal week, ventral retina first. It is the model in which AAV gene supplementation was first shown to restore cone vision.

cGMP is the channel's own ligand, and in the CNGA3-deficient retina it accumulates massively, peaking in the second and third postnatal weeks in mouse and tracking the wave of photoreceptor apoptosis. Removing retinal guanylyl cyclase 1 from the same background preserves cones, which places the accumulated cGMP, rather than the missing cation influx, upstream of most of the cell death. Protein kinase G activity rises with it. The same cones also fail to transport opsin into the outer segment and downregulate other phototransduction proteins.

evidence.reference_title: cGMP accumulation causes photoreceptor degeneration in CNG channel deficiency: evidence of cGMP cytotoxicity independently of enhanced CNG channel function.
evidence.snippet: In Cnga3(-/-);Gucy2e(-/-) mice lacking retGC1, cone density and expression levels of cone-specific proteins were significantly increased compared with Cnga3(-/-), consistent with a role of cGMP accumulation as the major contributor to cone death caused by CNG channel deficiency.

evidence.snippet: CNGA3(-/-) cones failed to transport opsins into outer segments, downregulated various proteins of the phototransduction cascade, and induced apoptotic death.

nodes.description: Progressive deterioration of cone function, as opposed to congenitally absent function, in the rare progressive subtype.

evidence.reference_title: CNGA3 mutations in hereditary cone photoreceptor disorders.
evidence.snippet: CNGA3 mutations were detected not only in patients with the complete form of achromatopsia but also in incomplete achromats with residual cone photoreceptor function and (rarely) in patients with evidence for severe progressive cone dystrophy.

nodes.description: The clinical outcome of silent cones, present from the first months of life: impaired colour discrimination along all three cone axes, poor visual acuity, photophobia with day blindness, and pendular nystagmus, on a background of preserved rod vision. Nystagmus and photophobia are what parents notice first, at a mean age under one year. Retinal function measured by microperimetry and contrast sensitivity is stable over years.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the genetic spectrum of achromatopsia: novel CNGA3 and CNGB3 variants.
evidence.snippet: Achromatopsia is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterised by congenital pendular nystagmus, photophobia, decreased visual acuity, and impaired colour vision.

nodes.description: A minority of CNGA3 substitutions are not loss-of-function at all. R410W sits in the gating ring, where the corresponding residue of the orthologous nematode TAX-4 channel contacts the S4 segment in the closed state; losing that contact destabilises the closed state and leaves the channel spontaneously open without cGMP. Spontaneously active channels kill cells, so these alleles damage cones by excess rather than absent channel activity. A further novel allele, Ser570Arg, is predicted by molecular dynamics to act the same way.

evidence.reference_title: Structural and functional characterization of an achromatopsia-associated mutation in a phototransduction channel.
evidence.snippet: CNGA3_R410W/CNGB3 and TAX4_R421W channels are spontaneously active without cGMP and induce cell death, suggesting cone degeneration triggered by spontaneous CNG channel activity as a possible cause of achromatopsia.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the genetic spectrum of achromatopsia: novel CNGA3 and CNGB3 variants.
evidence.snippet: Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that the CNGA3 c.1710C > A p.(Ser570Arg) variant may act as a gain-of-function variant, leading to altered cyclic nucleotide-gated channel activity in cone photoreceptors.

nodes.description: Cones lacking a functional CNG channel die by an endoplasmic reticulum stress-associated apoptotic pathway. On a cone-dominant background, CNGA3-deficient retina shows raised ER stress markers, calpain upregulation and caspase cleavage, together with nuclear translocation of apoptosis-inducing factor. In the CNGA3 knockout mouse the loss begins in the second postnatal week and clears the ventral retina first.

Cones are present but electrically silent: light-adapted and flicker electroretinogram responses are absent or nearly so while dark-adapted, rod-driven responses are preserved.

nodes.description: The native cone channel is a heterotetramer of CNGA3 and CNGB3 subunits in which CNGA3 carries the current. Without functional alpha subunits the cone outer segment has no cGMP-gated cation conductance: deleting the channel in mouse removes the cone photoresponse entirely, and in heterologous expression of two patient alleles only one formed a functioning channel at all, and then with grossly altered properties.

nodes.description: Over years the surviving foveal cones thin and their inner and outer segments break up, giving foveal thinning, ellipsoid-zone disruption and in some patients frank macular atrophy. Cross-sectional series show the outer-retinal stage worsening with age from early childhood, with no difference between CNGA3 and CNGB3. Longitudinal adaptive-optics imaging of CNGA3 patients over about 2.6 years finds the foveal cone mosaic stable, so the structural decline is slow enough that a wide therapeutic window remains.

evidence.snippet: Cone cell loss further progressed with age and occurred in 8 (42%) of 19 patients below 30 years and in 20 (95%) of 21 of those aged 30+ years.
